verse.text: The blessing of the LORD, it maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it.
verse.summary: Solomon sets this proverb right beside a warning about the slack hand and the diligent hand — so he isn't against hard work. He is telling you where the real increase comes from. Wealth chased in your own strength often arrives with sorrow attached: sleepless nights, broken relationships, a peace you can't buy back. But what God releases comes clean — no hidden debt, no grief stapled to it. If you've been toiling and taking nothing, rest your weight on His blessing today, and let Him add what your sweat alone could never hold.

sermon.title: Nevertheless at Thy Word
sermon.excerpt: Peter fished all night with every skill he had and came home with empty nets. Then a Carpenter told the fisherman where to throw — and one word of obedience, nevertheless at thy word, filled two boats until they began to sink.

bibleStudy.title: They Thought She Was Drunk

verses.text: So Hannah rose up after they had eaten in Shiloh, and after they had drunk. Now Eli the priest sat upon a seat by a post of the temple of the LORD. And she was in bitterness of soul, and prayed unto the LORD, and wept sore. And she vowed a vow, and said, O LORD of hosts, if thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of thine handmaid, and remember me, and not forget thine handmaid, but wilt give unto thine handmaid a man child, then I will give him unto the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor shall come upon his head. And it came to pass, as she continued praying before the LORD, that Eli marked her mouth. Now Hannah, she spake in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard: therefore Eli thought she had been drunken. And Eli said unto her, How long wilt thou be drunken? put away thy wine from thee. And Hannah answered and said, No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit: I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before the LORD. Count not thine handmaid for a daughter of Belial: for out of the abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto. Then Eli answered and said, Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition that thou hast asked of him. And she said, Let thine handmaid find grace in thy sight. So the woman went her way, and did eat, and her countenance was no more sad.

And Hannah prayed, and said, My heart rejoiceth in the LORD, mine horn is exalted in the LORD: my mouth is enlarged over mine enemies; because I rejoice in thy salvation. There is none holy as the LORD: for there is none beside thee: neither is there any rock like our God.

Others mocking said, These men are full of new wine. But Peter, standing up with the eleven, lifted up his voice, and said unto them, Ye men of Judaea, and all ye that dwell at Jerusalem, be this known unto you, and hearken to my words: For these are not drunken, as ye suppose, seeing it is but the third hour of the day.

bibleStudy.excerpt: Eli took one look at a woman pouring out her soul in silence and diagnosed her as drunk — the same mistake a Jerusalem crowd would make a thousand years later, watching men talk to God like He was actually listening.
body: Start at the table, not at the altar, because the table is where the wound actually gets reopened every single year. Hannah is married to a man who loves her — the text never once suggests otherwise — but he has a second wife named Peninnah who has children and Hannah does not, and Peninnah makes sure Hannah never forgets it, especially on feast days, especially at Shiloh, especially when everyone else's children are running around the tabernacle courtyard. So this particular year, after supper, Hannah does something she apparently hasn't done in quite this way before: she gets up while the family is still eating, walks to the tabernacle, and prays — not politely, not quietly composed, but "in bitterness of soul," weeping, making a vow. Eli the priest is sitting by the doorpost, the same seat he's probably sat in for decades, and he watches a grown woman come undone in front of the sanctuary of the living God. His conclusion, remarkably, is not "this woman is in pain." His conclusion is "this woman is drunk."

Look at what actually produced that diagnosis, because it isn't malice, it's just bad data: "Hannah, she spake in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard." No words came out. Just moving lips and a silence everyone could see but nobody could hear. That is prayer with every ornament stripped off — no eloquence, no King James cadence, not even an audible sentence, just a woman's whole case laid before God with nothing left to perform it with. Here's my real question for you today: when was the last time you prayed that honestly — so reduced, so wordless, so entirely between you and God — that a bystander would have had no category for what they were watching? Most of us pray loud enough to be understood by the room. Hannah prayed quiet enough that the room completely misread her.

Eli says it to her face: "How long wilt thou be drunken? put away thy wine from thee." A priest, trained his whole career to recognize the presence of God in that building, looks at the realest thing happening in it all week and calls it public drunkenness. I want you to notice Hannah's comeback, because it's a masterclass in how to answer somebody who has completely misjudged you: she doesn't get defensive, she doesn't storm out, she doesn't even argue theology. She just tells him the truth, plainly: "No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit: I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before the LORD." One sentence. No wine, no strong drink — only grief, poured out where grief belongs. You don't have to win every misreading with an argument. Sometimes you just tell the truth once, calmly, and let it stand.

Eli recovers fast and does the one thing he actually has the authority to do: he blesses her. "Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition that thou hast asked of him." And here's the detail that should stop you cold if you've ever waited on an answer that hadn't arrived yet: "the woman went her way, and did eat, and her countenance was no more sad." Read that again. No baby yet. No test result, no visible change, nothing anyone else in that tabernacle courtyard could point to. Her face changed before her circumstances did. That is not denial — that is what it actually looks like when a prayer lands in heaven before it shows up on earth. Faith doesn't wait for the evidence to smile first.

Fast-forward past the birth, past the weaning, past the morning Hannah hands her toddler to the very priest who once accused her of drunkenness and tells him the boy belongs to the house of the Lord now — and listen to what comes out of the same mouth that once made no sound at all: "My heart rejoiceth in the LORD, mine horn is exalted in the LORD: my mouth is enlarged over mine enemies; because I rejoice in thy salvation. There is none holy as the LORD." Mine mouth is enlarged. The lips that moved without a sound are now producing a song so theologically loaded that a teenage girl named Mary would reach for its structure a thousand years later to write her own. Same woman. Same mouth. Completely different volume — because the thing that kept the sound trapped inside her had finally been answered.

Now jump thirty-some generations forward to an upper room in Jerusalem, where a very different kind of noise is happening. A hundred and twenty believers, freshly filled with the Holy Ghost, are speaking in tongues they never learned, loud enough and strange enough that a crowd gathers outside wondering what on earth — or in heaven — is going on. And a watching world, faced with people genuinely overtaken by the presence of God, reaches for the exact same diagnosis Eli reached for a thousand years earlier: "Others mocking said, These men are full of new wine." Sit with the comedy of that for a second, because it's almost too neat to be an accident. Eli misread quiet prayer as drunkenness. Jerusalem misread loud praise as drunkenness. Same wrong verdict, opposite volume — which tells you the real problem was never the decibel level. The real problem is a watching world with no category left for people who are actually, uncut, in contact with God.

Peter's answer is Hannah's answer grown all the way up. He doesn't get embarrassed, he doesn't tone it down to make the crowd comfortable, and he doesn't skip the obvious joke sitting right there in the text: "these are not drunken, as ye suppose, seeing it is but the third hour of the day." Nine in the morning. Nobody — not even the most dedicated Jerusalem partygoer — is drunk by nine in the morning. Peter names the absurdity of the accusation and then does what Hannah didn't yet have the Scriptures to do: he opens the book and shows them this is Joel's prophecy landing exactly on schedule. Hannah answered with one true sentence about her own grief. Peter answers with one true sentence about his own joy, backed by the whole counsel of God. Same move. Bigger library.

Put the two scenes side by side and you've got a doctrine, not just a coincidence: real, unfiltered contact with God — whether it comes out as Hannah's silent travail or as a hundred and twenty people speaking in tongues at nine in the morning — will always look a little bit insane to a room that has never personally pressed its own anguish or its own joy all the way up to heaven. That's not a flaw in your prayer life. That's some of the oldest evidence there is that something actually happened. Nobody ever accused a comfortable, well-performed, three-minute prayer of being drunkenness. They only reach for that word when the thing in front of them is too real to file anywhere else.

So here's my real question for you today, and I want an honest answer, not a church answer: which one do you actually need right now — the courage to pray as honestly as Hannah did, even knowing the nearest Eli in your life might completely misread it, or the boldness to praise as loudly as that upper room did, even knowing somebody nearby is going to reach for "new wine" instead of new wine from heaven? Don't let either verdict talk you out of your own encounter. Hannah didn't argue Eli out of his opinion — she just kept pouring out her soul, and let heaven settle the matter later. Let it settle yours too.

God was never confused, not for one second, by either woman's volume, or by that whole room full of men speaking in tongues. He heard Hannah's unheard prayer as clearly as He heard Peter's sermon at the top of his voice, and He answered both the same way — with something the watching world couldn't have predicted and couldn't take credit for: a son named Samuel, which means "asked of God," and a church born in a single afternoon that has not stopped growing since. So pray how you need to pray today, even if it comes out as silence with moving lips. Praise how you need to praise today, even if somebody nearby thinks you've had too much. Heaven has never once mistaken either one for drunkenness. In Jesus' name, amen.

lines: Father, I declare today that my empty night is not my final report!
I have toiled and taken nothing — nevertheless, at Your word, I will let down the net!
My experience does not get the last vote. Your word does!
Jesus, I lend You my boat — my work, my home, my empty places — use them as You will!
I will not stay in the shallows of my own understanding. I launch out into the deep!
Whatsoever You say unto me, I will do it, even before it makes sense!
My nets will be filled, and my partners will be blessed with me!
The blessing of the LORD makes me rich, and He adds no sorrow with it!
What I could not catch all night, You are sending in one throw!
Save this. Speak it over your house today. Toiled all night? Nevertheless at His word — the nets are about to break! In Jesus' mighty name, amen!

dreamFire.title: Marked Only by the Blood
dreamFire.intro: Tonight's shield prayer is not aimed at one dream scene — it meets every mark, label, writing, garment, or seal an enemy hand tries to place on you between sleep and sunrise, wherever it was attempted and whatever symbol it wore. Pray it aloud before you close your eyes, and let every foreign mark be erased and answered by the Blood before you wake, in Jesus' name.
points: Father, Your Word declares in Galatians 6:17, "I bear in my body the marks of the Lord Jesus" — I carry only the mark of Jesus Christ tonight, and no other mark; every enemy stamp, seal, tattoo, or brand placed on me in any dream chamber is erased and nullified, in the mighty name of Jesus!

Lord, by the decree of Psalm 105:15, "Touch not mine anointed, and do my prophets no harm," I declare that every hand stretched out to mark me, brand me, or label me in the dream realm tonight is a hand that has touched what it was forbidden to touch — I command it to wither now, in the name of Jesus!

Father, Ephesians 1:13 declares that I am "sealed with that holy Spirit of promise" — every rival seal, every competing mark, every evil signature pressed upon me while I slept is overruled by the seal that already covers me; no second seal can stand where God has already sealed, in Jesus' mighty name!

I decree over every evil garment according to Revelation 7:14, "These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb" — every garment of mourning, confusion, sickness, or shame handed to me in a dream tonight is stripped off and washed white in that same blood, in the mighty name of Jesus!

Father, Your Word in Isaiah 61:10 declares, "he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness..." — I refuse every substitute garment measured for me in the dark, and I receive only what You have already clothed me in, in the mighty name of Jesus!

By the authority of Isaiah 54:17, "No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper; and every tongue that shall rise against thee in judgment thou shalt condemn," I condemn every tongue that spoke a mark over me tonight, and I declare that whatever weapon was formed against me in a dream has already failed, in Jesus' mighty name!

Father, You said in Luke 10:19, "Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall by any means hurt you" — I trample every serpent sent to bite, sting, or mark me in a dream tonight, and I declare that nothing assigned against me shall by any means hurt me, in the name of Jesus!

I decree by 1 John 4:4, "greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world" — every power that gathered to overpower me, overshadow me, or place its mark on me while I slept has met a greater One in me, and it is defeated before it begins, in the mighty name of Jesus!

Father, by Colossians 2:14, You have been "Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross" — every charge written against my name, every evil document signed over me in the dream realm tonight is blotted out and nailed to that same cross, in Jesus' mighty name!

I stand on Colossians 2:15, "having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it" — every principality that convened tonight to place a mark, a title, or a label upon me is openly put to shame, and I walk in that same triumph, in the mighty name of Jesus!

Father, as in Zechariah 3:3-4, when Joshua stood before the angel "clothed with filthy garments," You commanded, "Take away the filthy garments from him... I have caused thine iniquity to pass from thee, and I will clothe thee with change of raiment" — I command every filthy garment handed to me in a dream tonight to be stripped off, and I receive my change of raiment, in Jesus' mighty name!

So I decree over tonight, standing on Psalm 20:7-8, "Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the name of the LORD our God... They are brought down, and fallen: but we are risen, and stand upright" — every chariot of darkness assembled against me is brought down and fallen, while I rise and stand upright, marked only by the blood, untouched until sunrise, in the mighty, all-consuming name of Jesus Christ, amen! 🔥
